title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon with a full agenda.

Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order with commissioners quickly approving the agenda and consent agenda, the latter including past meeting minutes, the Warrant List for the first half of November, the Treasurer’s report for October, the October Police Activity Report, and the October Building and Zoning Report.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer congratulated the Flora Wolves Football Team. She thanked local businesses that donated to Saturday’s tailgate activities and for providing T-shirts for the playoffs.  Spicer also thanked the Flora Police Department, ESDA and the School Resource Officer for their participation in activities, noting that the SRO delivered the game football to the field.  She also provided a brief update on the downtown grants, explaining that personnel changes at the governing agency mean that the city will need to wait longer for additional updates. Spicer also mentioned in passing the status of other USDA projects.

The mayor also announced details for the annual Best Christmas Lights in Town contest, noting that this year’s contest will begin earlier than usual. Registration forms are available at City Hall and must be returned by December 4.  A separate story concerning the contest appears at wnoi.com.  Mayor Spicer also asked commissioners to approve $100 gift certificate to local restaurants for city employees for the holidays. Commissioners approved the measure unanimously.

Mayor Spicer then polled commissioners for their comments. Commissioner Phil Wiley asked the council to approve an ordinance adopting the wholesale connection agreement between the City of Flora, the Illinois Municipal Electric Agency (IMEA), and Ameren Services Company on behalf of Ameren Illinois. Commissioners approved the ordinance. Wiley then presented a second ordinance to approve an amendment to the Small Shipper Transportation Agreement between Trunkline Gas Company and the City of Flora.  Commissioners also approved that measure.  Wiley said the agreement helps keep utility prices stable for Flora residents. He also echoed the mayor’s praise for the Wolves football team, calling their effort part of a great season, and thanked everyone…businesses and patron taking part in the pre-game tailgating. He also thanked parents for supporting their student-athletes for so many years at both home games and those on the road.

Commissioner Jim Fehrenbacher also congratulated the Wolves and joined the others in recognizing the team’s successful season.

City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford asked commissioners to reject the bids for the Public Works building remodel. He said the bids came in 30 percent higher than budgeted, ranging from $110,000 to $118,000. Commissioners agreed to reject the bids.  The council then approved payment of $446,289 to Hutchinson Recreation and Design for playground equipment and its installation at Rotary Park as part of the OSLAD Grant. Stanford noted the price was locked in before an increase took effect. Commissioners also approved an ordinance for a professional services agreement with Milano and Grunloh Engineers of Effingham for water main system improvements totaling $243,966.  Half of that is to cover engineering services and the remaining half covers project management service.  Finally, the council approved an ordinance authorizing the city to borrow $1,954,199 from the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency’s Public Water Supply Loan Program. The 30-year loan is also eligible for up to 30 percent of the amount to qualify for loan forgiveness.

Building and Zoning Official Chad Bales asked the council to grant a variance to Paul Duquaine at 303 Lincoln Avenue for the construction of a three-unit apartment complex. Commissioners approved the variance. Commissioner Wiley thanked Duquesne for investing in the community.

Superintendent of Public Services Toby Reinhart requested authorization for contract changes on the Safe Routes to School project. The changes increase the contract with Kiefer Brothers Construction of Mount Carmel by $7,976 to balance quantities. Commissioners approved the request. They also authorized Reinhart to seek bids for a gas department service truck and an electric department service truck.

title: GALBRAITH SENTENCING
full_story:
Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip M. Givens announced that Amber N. Galbraith, 38, of Flora; was sentenced to time in the Illinois Department of Corrections on Monday, in Clay County Circuit Court.

Galbraith pled guilty to the charge of Unlawful Possession of Methamphetamine, a Class X Felony, on August 26th.  The charges alleged that Galbraith knowingly possessed baggies containing methamphetamine weighing more than 100 grams on April 12th, 2025.  Galbraith received a sentence of 10 years in the Illinois Department of Corrections by Judge Joel Powless.  She will have an 18-month period of Mandatory Supervised Release to follow.

The investigation was conducted by the Clay County Sheriff’s Office.  State’s Attorney Phillip Givens said: “My office continues to hold people accountable for bringing Methamphetamine into our community.  We are grateful to have Law Enforcement working diligently with us to combat Methamphetamine, especially in such large quantities.  We are lucky to have such hardworking law enforcement working together to look out for the best interest of justice”.

title: TURNER SENTENCING
full_story:
Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip M. Givens announced that Cody A. Turner, 38, of Clay City; was sentenced to time in the Illinois Department of Corrections on Monday, in Clay County Circuit Court.

Turner pled guilty to the charge of Unlawful Possession of a Stolen License Plate, a Class 2 Felony, on July 27th.  The charges alleged that Turner possessed a license plate knowing it to have been stolen on April 25th.  After a contested sentencing hearing, Turner received a sentence of 3 years in the Illinois Department of Corrections, by Judge Joel Powless.  He will have a 1-year period of Mandatory Supervised Release to follow.

The investigation was conducted by the Flora Police Department and assisted by the Clay County Sheriff’s Office.  State’s Attorney Phillip Givens said: “The “Safe-T” Act may place certain offenses under certain presumptions when it comes to accountability.  But if you continue to break the law, then we will hold you accountable.  We are grateful to work alongside our Law Enforcement Officers who feel just as strongly as we do”.

title: BEST CHRISTMAS LIGHTS IN TOWN CONTEST
full_story:
The City of Flora is getting ready to brighten up the holiday season, and local officials are making a few changes to this year’s annual “Best Christmas Lights in Town” contest.

The city is moving up both the registration deadline and the judging period.  They say the earlier schedule gives them time to compile a list of participating homes so the whole community can drive around, enjoy the displays, and even cast a vote for their favorites.

If you’d like to enter your home, pick up an application at Flora City Hall and once completed, drop it off at city hall by 4:00pm on Friday, December 4th.  Judges tour from 7:00-10:00 pm on December 14th through 17th.  The city announces the winners at the December 21st City Council meeting, and they ask that all participants keep their displays lit through January 1st.

Top decorators will earn a break on their winter utility bill.  First place takes home a 150-dollar utility credit, second place wins a100-dollar bill credit, and third place gets a 75-dollar credit which will apply directly to their February 2027 utility bills.  Please note that city employees are not eligible to enter.

title: SCOUTING FOR FOOD
full_story:
Saturday is pick up day for the Flora Boy Scout Troop 8282 and Louisville Cub Scout Pack 295 “Scouting for Food” annual nonperishable food collection.

If you would like to provide nonperishable food items, please place those items in the blue bags that the boy scouts distributed last Saturday.  If you did not receive a bag or need additional bags you can place items in other bags or boxes and place those on your front porch for pickup this Saturday.

The food collected will be taken to the Clay County food pantry for their normal distribution.

The Boy Scouts will be selling Christmas Trees again this year.  Starting on Friday November 27th the scouts will be set up at Dickeys Rentals across from Napa.  The scouts will only have around 50 trees this year, so don’t wait.  The scouts will also be selling homemade baked goods during the tree sales while supplies last.  Proceeds will help send the scouts to Philmont Scout Ranch in 2027.

title: WEEZ TO BE INDUCTED
full_story:
Wayne County Press sportswriter Brian “Weez” Turner has been selected for induction into the Illinois Basketball Coaches Association Hall of Fame as a member of its Class of 2027.

Turner, who has covered Fairfield Community High School athletics for the Wayne County Press since 2005, will be inducted in the media category during ceremonies May 1 at CEFCU Arena on the campus of Illinois State University in Normal.

The recognition caps a journalism career spanning more than three decades in print, radio and television throughout southern and central Illinois.

Turner’s journalism career began in 1993 as a member of The Locust Log, the student newspaper at Flora High School. His first professional news-paper experience came the following summer, when he worked as a darkroom technician for the Clay County Advocate-Press.

He moved into broadcasting in 1997, joining WNOI radio and television in Flora. During his three years there, Turner worked behind the camera and handled production duties for the station’s high school football and basketball broadcasts, working alongside radio broadcast crews from Salem, Effingham, Flora, Newton and Olney.

The IBCA Hall of Fame, established in 1973, recognizes individuals who have made significant contributions to basketball throughout Illinois, including coaches, players, officials, media members and other contributors.

The Class of 2027 will be honored May 1, with a reception beginning at 2:30 p.m. and the induction banquet following at 5:30 p.m. at CEFCU Arena in Normal.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
With 99% of soybeans and 96% of corn harvested in Illinois, according to USDA’s November 16th crop progress and condition report, most farmers across the state are reflecting on the growing season.

There were 5.9 days suitable for field work during the week ending November 15th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 45.7 degrees, 2.2 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 0.12 inches, 0.61 inches below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 16% very short, 34% short, 46% adequate, and 4% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 19% very short, 36% short, 42% adequate, and 3% surplus.

Corn harvested reached 96%, equal to the 5-year average.  Soybeans harvested reached 99%, compared to the 5-year average of 97%.

Winter wheat planted reached 97% ahead of the 5-year average of 93%.  Winter wheat emerged reached 81%, compared to the 5-year average of 79%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 3% very poor, 5% poor, 28% fair, 53% good, and 11% excellent.

title: NATIONAL TEST
full_story:
Residents across Illinois, Minnesota and Wisconsin can expect a brief interruption to radio and television programming today, for a scheduled test of the Emergency Alert System.

At approximately 1:20 pm, radio and television broadcasters, cable systems, satellite radio and television providers, and wireline video providers nationwide will interrupt normal programming to relay a test message.  The message will clearly state that this is only a test and that no action is required by the public.  When the test has concluded, normal programming will resume.

“During an emergency, every second is crucial,” said FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton.  “FEMA’s alert and warning systems ensure that no second is wasted getting you the critical information needed to keep you safe.  Operational tests, like todays, allow us to identify and fix potential issues before an actual emergency occurs.”

FEMA’s Emergency Alert System is a national public warning system made up of thousands of radio, television, cable, satellite and wireline video providers.  Through the Emergency Alert System, the President can address the American people or share life-saving information with the public during a national emergency.  FEMA is required by law to conduct a nationwide test of the public alert and warning system at least once every three years.  These tests allow FEMA to identify technical or operational issues before the system is needed during an actual emergency.

If the test cannot be conducted today, the backup date is Thursday, December 3rd.

For more information, visit the 2026 Nationwide Emergency Alert System Test webpage on FEMA.gov.
